content:
maya: Heads up, seeing sharp rise in 5xx from edge proxies and kube nodes failing model pulls. Looks like NAT port exhaustion in us-west-2 AZ-b. 

sam: On it, any dashboards/links?

ops-bot: alert: egress_natsaturation_high (threshold 0.8) triggered for us-west-2-b at 06:12 UTC. See grafana: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/egress/egress-nat-az?view=us-west-2-b

jordan: Confirmed from agent logs: repeated ESTABLISHED -> TIME_WAIT and then connection reset on our model-pull tasks. Pods OOM? no, socket errors. Example error from model-fetcher: `dial tcp 10.0.0.1:443: connect: connection refused` spams, but underlying reason is SNAT failures.

leo: Symptoms match ephemeral port depletion: many short-lived outbound connections when autoscaler spins up GPU nodes and they pull ~20-40 model shards each. We only have one NAT gateway per AZ right now.

anika: Immediate mitigation ideas: 1) throttle concurrent model pulls per node 2) enable S3 VPC endpoints so model files don't go via NAT 3) spin up a second NAT gateway in the same AZ (fast but costly).

maya: Throttling config? Can we patch model-fetcher to exponential backoff + connection pooling quickly?

jordan: We can gate persistence: switch to HTTP/2 multiplexing for model pulls (single connection per worker) — needs small client change but could take a day. Quick patch: limit concurrent downloads to 4 per node via env var.

sam: Deploying a rolling config to GPU ASG to add `MAX_CONCURRENT_PULLS=4` now. Will push canary to 3 nodes first.

ops-bot: deploy: model-fetcher/config v2.3.1 -> canary on gpu-asg-usw2b (3 nodes).

leo: Also recommending immediate network change: bring up an extra NAT gateway in AZ-b and enable route table to use both via NLB? AWS LB for egress not ideal. Spinning a second NAT will roughly double available ports.

anika: Confirmed cost tradeoff: ~+$600/mo per extra NAT gw. For incidents it's acceptable.

maya: Another low-effort hack: enable source port range increase on node OS? We can tweak `net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range` to broaden ephemeral ports from `32768-60999` to `10240-65535`. That helps but not a long term fix (conn tracking still a limit). Ops: can we roll kernel param on GPU AMI quickly?

sam: I can change it via user-data and trigger a rolling reboot, but rebooting GPUs during peak is risky. Maybe do it for a small canary ASG first.

jordan: Also, conntrack table exhaustion shows up in `conntrack -S` output. Snippet from node: ```conntrack entries: 65535 used, max: 65536 tcp: 54000 (established 12000, time_wait 30000)``` so hitting conntrack limit too. Need to bump `nf_conntrack_max` and tune `nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_time_wait`.

leo: Bumping conntrack + ephemeral range buys time. Long term fixes: 1) introduce egress pooling proxy (node-local or central) that does keepalive and connection reuse 2) S3/EFS direct endpoints for model artifacts 3) pre-warm model caches in a daemonset so top-of-scale pulls are staggered.

anika: I can draft a rollout plan for an egress-proxy using envoy with HTTP/2 upstream pooling and connection reuse. Would be a week of eng effort + infra.

maya: For short term action items: (A) throttle concurrent pulls (sam) (B) deploy second NAT gw in AZ-b (ops) (C) enable S3 endpoint for model buckets (infra sec) (D) canary bump conntrack on 2 nodes (sam).

sam: Starting A now. Opening PR for conntrack sysctl change, will run canary on two idle GPU nodes.

ops-bot: incident-note: created incident INC-2026-231, tagged `egress-nat-saturation`. Pager duty: @oncall infra.

leo: After A and C we should see immediate drop in new SYNs. I'll monitor SYN rate and ephemeral usage.

jordan: One oddity: control-plane requests to internal image registry also ride the same NAT and are contending. We should move registry to VPC-private or use ECR VPC endpoint.

anika: I'll prioritize adding ECR + S3 endpoints to the infra terraform change set. Low risk.

maya: Update: canary with MAX_CONCURRENT_PULLS=4 reduced failed pulls from 12% -> 2% on canary nodes in 20m. Good. Sam, proceed with wider rollout if no regressions.

sam: Rolling to remaining 24 GPU nodes now, 2 at a time. ETA 40m.

ops-bot: cloudwatch: NAT port usage graph shows 75% drop after canary change on canary subnets.

leo: Spinning up extra NAT as discussed. Provisioning now (will update route table to prefer new gw for subset of subnets).

jordan: Postmortem note: autoscaler + parallel model shard pulls = short-lived fanout causing ephemeral port avalanche. Need to adjust autoscaler or use staggered pulls. Add to eng backlog: staggered-pull-controller.

anika: Long-term proposal doc: `docs/egress/egress-proxy-and-pool.md` — I'll start a draft and share. It will include performance numbers for HTTP/2 vs HTTP/1.1, conntrack tuning, and cost estimates for NAT replicas vs egress proxies.

maya: Great. Closing immediate incident if metrics stay stable after full rollout. Leaving this thread for follow-ups and the doc link. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: incident INC-2026-231 status -> monitoring.

leo: Post-incident checklist: - complete ECR/S3 endpoints change - implement connection pooling proxy design - add autoscaler throttle knobs - run chaos test (simulate burst model-pulls)

jordan: I'll own the chaos test and stagged-pull controller spike.

anika: I'll own the egress-proxy RFC.

sam: I'll own the sysctl/conntrack roll plan and emergency NAT gw runbook.

maya: Thanks all. If anyone sees recurrences ping this thread.

ops-bot: note: incident resolved? still monitoring.
